protein_identifier.protein_name: Segment polarity protein dishevelled homolog DVL-1

isoforms.description: Alternative splicing variant with sequence variation at positions 378-403
isoforms.sequence: Isoform 2 contains glutamic acid substitution at specified region

domains_and_motifs.name: DIX domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Domain present in Dishevelled and Axin; mediates homooligomerization and heterotypic interactions with Axin DIX domain. Critical for Wnt signaling pathway activation.

sources.notes: Domain present in Dishevelled and axin

domains_and_motifs.name: Dishevelled-specific domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Central region unique to Dishevelled proteins; contains multiple phosphorylation sites and basic residues. Subject to extensive phosphorylation by casein kinases.

domains_and_motifs.name: PDZ domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Protein-protein interaction domain that binds to C-terminal motifs in Frizzled receptors (KTxxxW motif) and other signaling partners. Forms homotrimers in crystal structures. Binding site for small molecule inhibitors.

sources.notes: PDZ domain (also known as DHR or GLGF)

domains_and_motifs.name: DEP domain
domains_and_motifs.description: Dishevelled/EGL-10/Pleckstrin domain; mediates interaction with cell membrane and is involved in planar cell polarity signaling. Required for membrane localization upon Wnt stimulation.

domains_and_motifs.name: Dishevelled C-terminal domain
domains_and_motifs.description: C-terminal region of Dishevelled; largely disordered with low complexity and proline-rich sequences. Contains the PGXPP degron motif recognized by KLHL12 E3 ubiquitin ligase.

domains_and_motifs.name: PGXPP degron motif
domains_and_motifs.description: Degron motif recognized by KLHL12 E3 ubiquitin ligase for proteasomal degradation. Contains PGXPP consensus sequence. Adopts U-shaped turn conformation when bound to KLHL12 Kelch domain.

sources.notes: Identified by crystallography; Kd = 22.3 μM binding to KLHL12

domains_and_motifs.name: Frizzled C-terminal binding site
domains_and_motifs.description: PDZ domain binding groove that recognizes KTxxxW motif in the C-terminus of Frizzled receptors. Critical for Wnt signal transduction from membrane to cytoplasm.

sources.notes: Direct binding to Frizzled C-terminal motif; affinity ~3-4 μM
Binding site for frizzled family members

domains_and_motifs.name: Casein kinase phosphorylation sites
domains_and_motifs.description: Multiple serine and threonine residues phosphorylated by casein kinase 1 epsilon (CSNK1E) and casein kinase 2 (CSNK2). Phosphorylation regulates DVL1 activity and membrane translocation. S194 phosphorylation enhances ARRB1 interaction.

sources.notes: Phosphorylation at Ser-194 by casein kinases
Sequential phosphorylation by CK1 epsilon regulates Wnt pathway activation

domains_and_motifs.name: Nuclear localization signal
domains_and_motifs.description: Basic region that mediates nuclear translocation, enhanced by interaction with FOXK2. Important for DVL1 nuclear functions in transcriptional regulation.

sources.notes: DVL1 requires nuclear localization for proliferation regulation

experimental_structures.description: Crystal structure of human Dishevelled1 PDZ domain homotrimer. Shows unique trimeric assembly with C3 cyclic symmetry where β2-β3 loops occupy canonical ligand-binding clefts, forming auto-inhibitory trimer.
Crystal structure of human Dishevelled1 PDZ domain with its inhibitor NPL3009. High-resolution structure showing small molecule binding in PDZ groove.

Crystal structure of the kelch domain of human KLHL12 in complex with DVL1 peptide (residues 650-669). Shows PGXPP degron motif in U-shaped turn conformation bound to KLHL12 β-propeller domain. Demonstrates molecular basis for ubiquitin-mediated degradation.

alphafold_prediction.confidence_summary: High confidence (pLDDT > 70) for structured domains: DIX (1-85), PDZ (251-339), DEP (425-499). Low confidence (pLDDT < 50) for disordered regions: basic/phosphorylation region (90-247), C-terminal domain (503-695). These predictions align with known domain architecture and experimental disorder predictions.

post_translational_modifications.function: Enhances ARRB1 (beta-arrestin-1) interaction; regulates DVL1 activity in Wnt signaling

Multiple constitutive and Wnt-induced phosphorylation sites in basic/PDZ region by casein kinase 1 epsilon (CSNK1E) and casein kinase 2 (CSNK2). More than 50 sites identified across DVL family members. Sequential phosphorylation activates DVL and triggers membrane translocation.

Both Lys-48-linked (degradation signal) and Lys-63-linked (signaling) polyubiquitin chains. KLHL12 E3 ligase mediates Lys-48 ubiquitination via PGXPP degron recognition. CYLD deubiquitinase removes ubiquitin to stabilize DVL1.
Two O-linked glycosylation sites documented; functional significance unclear

function.uniprot_function: Participates in Wnt signaling by binding to the cytoplasmic C-terminus of frizzled family members and transducing the Wnt signal to down-stream effectors. Plays a role both in canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling. Implicated in the signal transduction pathways mediated by multiple Wnt genes. Required for LEF1 activation upon WNT1 or WNT3A stimulation. Forms a ternary complex with MUSK and PAK1 that is important for MUSK-dependent regulation of AChR clustering during the formation of the neuromuscular junction. May play a role in hair cell orientation in the inner ear and neuromuscular junction development.
function.catalytic_activity: Not an enzyme; functions as a scaffold and signal transduction adaptor protein
subcellular_location: Nucleus (upon interaction with FOXK2 or during Wnt signaling)
Wnt signalosome (membrane-associated puncta upon pathway activation)
function.tissue_specificity: Widely expressed. Found in brain, heart, kidney, liver, lung, skeletal muscle, pancreas, and placenta. Expression in multiple embryonic and adult tissues consistent with roles in development and tissue homeostasis.

biological_process.term: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

reactome.pathway_name: TCF dependent signaling in response to WNT

kegg.pathway_name: Signaling pathways regulating pluripotency of stem cells

pathways.pathway_role_summary: DVL1 is a central hub protein in Wnt signaling pathways. In canonical Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, DVL1 transduces signals from Frizzled receptors to the beta-catenin destruction complex, ultimately leading to beta-catenin stabilization and nuclear translocation for TCF/LEF-mediated transcription. In non-canonical pathways (Wnt/PCP and Wnt/Ca2+), DVL1 activates distinct downstream effectors including DAAM1, RhoA, and PKC to regulate cell polarity, cytoskeletal organization, and calcium signaling. DVL1 activity is regulated by multiple mechanisms: phosphorylation by casein kinases activates the protein, ubiquitination by KLHL12 targets it for degradation, and deubiquitination by CYLD stabilizes it. DVL1 also has specialized non-Wnt functions including neuromuscular junction development via MUSK-PAK1 complex formation.

disease_associations.description: Rare skeletal dysplasia syndrome characterized by dysmorphic facial features resembling fetal face, mesomelic limb shortening, genital hypoplasia, and renal anomalies. Multiple frameshift mutations cluster in the penultimate exon of DVL1. Caused by heterozygous mutations that likely result in haploinsufficiency or dominant-negative effects on Wnt signaling.

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive dataset with high-quality experimental evidence. Structural information available for PDZ domain (X-ray crystallography) and KLHL12-binding degron. AlphaFold prediction available for full-length protein showing expected domain architecture. Extensive interaction data from multiple databases with good convergence. Quantitative kinetic data limited: available for KLHL12-degron binding (Kd = 22.3 μM), FZD PDZ binding (~3-4 μM), and PDZ domain small molecule inhibitors. Enzymatic parameters (Km, Kcat) for casein kinase phosphorylation not available. PTM sites well-characterized, especially phosphorylation (>50 sites identified across DVL family). Disease association clearly established for Robinow syndrome.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: DVL1 is a critical signal transduction node in Wnt signaling pathways, making it essential for modeling canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling networks. Key modeling considerations: (1) Multiple regulatory mechanisms including phosphorylation-based activation, ubiquitination-mediated degradation, and deubiquitination-mediated stabilization; (2) Oligomerization dynamics via DIX domain forming higher-order assemblies; (3) Membrane recruitment upon pathway activation; (4) Multiple binding partners with distinct functional outcomes (activation, inhibition, scaffolding); (5) Tissue-specific expression and nuclear/cytoplasmic shuttling. Limited quantitative kinetic data for most interactions represents a challenge for detailed kinetic modeling, though qualitative network topology is well-established. The protein's multi-domain architecture with distinct functional modules (DIX for oligomerization, PDZ for receptor binding, DEP for membrane interaction) suggests modular modeling approach would be appropriate.
